title: El Salvador: Authorities remain silent over request for humanitarian visit to Ruth López
content:
As human rights defender Ruth López spends her second birthday behind bars, Amnesty International reiterates its request to the Salvadoran authorities to conduct a humanitarian visit and calls for her immediate and unconditional release.

On 1 August 2026, Amnesty International sent formal communications to the Attorney General, the Minister of Justice and Public Security, the Director General of Prisons, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the judge in charge of the case, requesting authorization for a high-level delegation from the organization to visit Ruth López and directly assess her conditions of detention. The request was reiterated on 26 August and, to date, none of the five authorities has responded. Ana Piquer, Amnesty International’s Americas Director, said:

The authorities’ silence appears increasingly deliberate with each passing day. Every minute that passes makes it even more necessary to allow an independent assessment of Ruth’s conditions in prison.”

Ana Piquer, Amnesty International’s Americas Director

title: Azerbaijan: Authorities must immediately release activist Bahruz Samadov who cut himself during latest court appearance
content:
Reacting to reports that imprisoned Azerbaijani researcher and peace activist Bahruz Samadov harmed himself during a Supreme Court hearing on 25 September, Natalia Nozadze, Amnesty International’s South Caucasus Researcher, said:

“Azerbaijani authorities are obliged to protect and fulfil Bahruz Samadov’s right to health while he remains unjustly imprisoned. While they continue to deny him access to adequate healthcare, including mental health support, his health condition is worsening. The denial of health care, and the restrictions on family contact, may amount to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment, contrary to Azerbaijan’s international human rights obligations.”

“Bahruz Samadov should not have been imprisoned in the first place. He is serving a 15-year sentence on fabricated ‘high treason’ charges stemming from his peaceful activism, journalism and advocacy for dialogue with Armenia. The Azerbaijani authorities must release him immediately and unconditionally.”

Background

On 25 September, Bahruz Samadov used a sharp object to cut his right arm several times during a break in a Supreme Court hearing on 25 September, according to his lawyer, Zibeyda Sadigova.

title: Austria: “End Genocide” protest at UEFA Nations League Israel game
content:
As the group phase of the 2026/27 men’s UEFA Nations League kicked off tonight, during the Austria vs Israel football match in Linz, Amnesty International Austria displayed a  banner inside the stadium saying: “END GENOCIDE”. 

Amnesty International is calling on UEFA and FIFA to suspend the Israel Football Association (IFA), due to clear evidence that it continues to support illegal Israeli settlements in the Occupied Palestinian Territory (OPT). 

Our protest is directed against many governments and sporting authorities that know exactly what is happening in the Gaza Strip and still do nothing

Alexander Weihrauch, Campaigner at Amnesty International Austria

Our protest is directed against many governments and sporting authorities that know exactly what is happening in the Gaza Strip and still do nothing

“Today, thousands of people watched the Austria vs Israel match in Linz. For a moment, we directed their gaze towards Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, where death and suffering continue despite the so-called ceasefire.

title: Yemen: One year on, Huthis must release arbitrarily detained lawyer Abdul Majid Sabra
content:
One year ago on 25 September 2025, the Huthi de facto authorities in Sana’a arbitrarily detained prominent lawyer and human rights defender Abdul Majid Sabra. In response, Diala Haidar, Amnesty International’s Yemen Researcher, said: 

“Abdul Majid Sabra, a lawyer who dedicated his career to defending those detained based on the peaceful exercise of their human rights, continues to be arbitrarily detained at the Huthi-run Security and Intelligence detention centre in Chamlan. He was arrested from his office a day ahead of the anniversary of Yemen’s 26th of September Revolution, a date the Huthis oppose celebrating. According to a relative, he was interrogated about his social media posts marking the anniversary and about his profession as a human rights lawyer. To date, he has not been formally charged.

title: USA: Amnesty International Calls for ICE to Be Abolished After Documenting Widespread Human Rights Violations in Anti-Immigrant Operations
content:
In a new report released today, Amnesty International documented widespread human rights violations committed by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and other federal agencies during the Trump administration’s large-scale, militarized immigration enforcement operations in Chicago, Minneapolis-St. Paul, New Orleans and Washington, DC.

The report, “We Had Whistles, They Had Guns”: Human Rights Violations in U.S. Immigration Enforcement Operations and the Case to Abolish ICE, demonstrates that the Trump administration is implementing a mass detention and deportation system, fueled by racist, xenophobic and false narratives, whose objective is to detain and deport as many migrants, asylum seekers and refugees from the United States as possible and spread fear throughout immigrant communities more broadly.

title: Europe: Sale of Israel Bonds finally ends in Europe
content:
Reacting to the Central Bank of Ireland’s confirmation that on the expiry of the Israel Bonds’ prospectus their sale in Europe has ended Stephen Cockburn, Amnesty International’s Europe Director, said: 

“This outcome is a testament to the indefatigable campaigners who protested outside the Central Bank for more than a year, supported by the Parliamentarians who kept pushing for Ireland’s compliance with international law in the halls of power, and all those who spoke out against these Bonds’ sale in Europe.

Today’s confirmation of the end of Israel Bonds’ sale in Europe shows just what this solidarity can achieve

Steve Cockburn, Europe Director at Amnesty International

Today’s confirmation of the end of Israel Bonds’ sale in Europe shows just what this solidarity can achieve

“States have a clear obligation to act to end Israel’s violations against Palestinians. Rejecting any involvement in Israel’s genocide, apartheid and other international crimes, requires courage and conviction as states in Europe continue to crackdown on this vital activism.

title: 38 Global Civil Society Organizations file joint brief in US lawsuit challenging legality of Trump’s ICC sanctions
content:
The Trump administration’s escalating campaign against the International Criminal Court (ICC) is reaching far beyond the judges, prosecutors, and human rights groups it has sanctioned, chilling civil society engagement with the Court and undermining victims’ access to justice, Amnesty International, the International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH), and 36 other Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) said today.

We will not sit back and let President Trump destroy the Rome Statute

Agnès Callamard, Secretary General of Amnesty International

title: Venezuela: Three months after the two earthquakes, a human rights-centred response remains absent
content:
On 24 June 2026, two earthquakes measuring 7.2 and 7.5 in magnitude struck northern Venezuela, causing one of the country’s most serious disasters in recent decades. According to official figures, 6,509 people were killed and 60,785 affected homes were assessed, of which 11,001 were classified as high risk.

“Three months after these events, there remains a debt to those affected that must be addressed by placing their human rights and dignity at the centre of the recovery,” said Ana Piquer, Amnesty International’s Americas Director.

title: Ecuador: Militarization Continues and the Armed Forces Still Refuse to Cooperate
content:
One year after the publication of the report “It was the military. I Saw Them“, which documented the enforced disappearance of 10 people from the Ecuadorian coast, including six children, in the context of President Daniel Noboa’s so-called “Plan Fenix”, some progress has been made. Nevertheless, the lack of cooperation by the Armed Forces in the criminal investigations and the deepening of the policy of militarization of the public security continue to be the main obstacles preventing all victims’ families from obtaining truth, justice, and reparation, and from ensuring the non-repetition of these crimes, Amnesty International said today. 

“The progress achieved over the past year demonstrates that it is possible to respond to the demands for truth and justice made by the families, civil society, and international mechanisms. Yet this progress remains insufficient as long as many of those families continue not knowing what happened to their loved ones and the military authorities continue to withhold essential information for the investigations,” said Ana Piquer, Regional Director for the Americas of Amnesty International.

title: South Sudan: Authorities must protect civic space ahead of scheduled national elections
content:
Following the announced dissolution of South Sudan’s Revitalized Transitional Government of National Unity, a decisive step towards the country’s first-ever elections scheduled for 22 December, Amnesty International’s Regional Director for East and Southern Africa, Tigere Chagutah, said:

“Ahead of these long-awaited and historic elections, South Sudanese authorities must ensure that a conducive environment exists for people to vote and stand in elections, including respect for and enjoyment of human rights, and freedom from discrimination and arbitrary or unnecessary and disproportionate restrictions.

“The legitimacy of any election depends not only on whether it is held, but on whether people can exercise their rights freely, safely and equally. For years, Amnesty International and other organizations have documented the repressive tactics deployed by the South Sudanese authorities to silence dissent, detain critics, and restrict freedom of expression and the right to protest.

title: Europe: Israel’s participation in the UEFA Nations League is a betrayal of Palestinians, football’s own rules and human rights
content:
Ahead of the opening matches of the 2026/27 men’s UEFA Nations League group phase where Austria, Ireland and Kosovo will play against Israel during the 24 September – 6 October international window, Steve Cockburn, Amnesty International’s Regional Director for Europe said: 

“It’s unconscionable that the Israel men’s football team will participate in the UEFA Nations League this autumn despite clear evidence that Israel’s football association continues to support illegal settlements.

“Instead of sending a clear message that there is a cost for Israel’s unlawful occupation of the Occupied Palestinian Territory (OPT) and its atrocity crimes against Palestinians, UEFA is giving Israel an international stage as it maintains its brutal occupation of the OPT, its system of apartheid over all Palestinians, and its ongoing genocide against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip.

title: Türkiye’s crackdown on LGBTI groups and activists is part of an escalating rights crisis
content:
On 13 September, I woke in southwest Türkiye to news of a large-scale operation targeting LGBTI organizations and human rights defenders across the country. Since then, police have arrested at least 116 people across 15 provinces following raids on homes, venues and the offices of LGBTI rights organizations. At least 83 people have been placed in pretrial detention and criminal investigations have been launched against more than 160 people. LGBTI rights organisations have reported allegations of intrusive strip searches, insults and humiliation as well as HRDs being held in isolation in violation of their rights. Hundreds of social media accounts belonging to LGBTI organizations and activists, journalists, media outlets and others have so far been blocked or restricted alongside a number of websites. Those affected include Amnesty International Türkiye’s X account.  

As protest within Türkiye builds and international condemnation mounts, it is clear that the Turkish authorities have every intention of intensifying the crackdown

Milena Buyum, Amnesty International
